html:
Intercommunal fighting broke out in Cyprus on 21 December 1963, known to Turkish Cypriots as Bloody Christmas, after Makarios proposed changes to the power sharing constitution of 1960.

Greek Cypriot irregulars and police attacked Turkish Cypriot quarters, and hundreds died on both sides. About 25,000 Turkish Cypriots fled into armed enclaves, and Turkish Cypriot ministers left the government. A British officer drew a Green Line across Nicosia that still divides the city. In 1964 the United Nations sent a peacekeeping force that is still on the island. The fighting ended the shared state in practice, and Cyprus has been divided along these lines in one way or another ever since.
sum: Intercommunal fighting broke out in Cyprus on 21 December 1963, known to Turkish Cypriots as Bloody Christmas, after Makarios proposed changes to the power sharing constitution of 1960.
